definition: Languid means sluggish from fatigue or weakness.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word languid. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know languid should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Jet lag left the whole crew languid, drifting through the soundcheck a half beat behind the drummer.
Relaxed is the pleasant, milder state next to languid — muscles loose by choice, energy still on call the moment it's wanted, while languid limbs are heavy because the strength just isn't there.
Exhausted goes further than relaxed—an exhausted hiker has nothing left at all, while a languid one still drifts forward at half speed.

Listless is flatness of interest — the listless have energy they can't be bothered to spend, pushing food around the plate. Languid is flatness of strength: heavy limbs, a drifting pace, a body at half power. A listless person could move and doesn't care to; a languid one barely can.

Sluggish describes anything slow to start and slow to move — cold syrup, morning traffic, an old laptop — without saying why. Languid is for living bodies drained by fatigue or weakness, and it can even sound graceful: a languid wave, a languid stroll. Sluggish never flatters; languid sometimes does.
